source.quote: Shanling's own announcement for the H5, read 2026-11-25; the product page /product/434 is 21 image slices. Two adjacent lines in the Specification, verbatim: « USB Input Hi-Res Support：32 bit / 768 kHz， DSD 512 » and « MicroSD Hi-Res Support：32 bit / 384 kHz， DSD 256 » - the full-width colons and commas are the page's. Also: « Digital Filters：6 Preset Filters »; « DAC：2x AKM AK4493SEQ » (while the bullet list above says « Pair of AKM AK4493S DACs »); « - USB, Coaxial, Optical, Bluetooth input »; « - Xmos XU316 USB chip »; « Storage： MicroSD Card Slot, up to 2TB »; « Gain Setting: Three Level Setting »; « Bluetooth 5.0 Receiver »; « Bluetooth Codec Support: LDAC / AAC / SBC »; « Audio formats: DSD(".iso",".dsf",".dff") / ISO / DXD / APE / FLAC / WAV / AIFF / AlF / DTS / MP3 / WMA / AAC / OGG / ALAC / MP2 / M4A / AC3 / M3U / M3U8/ OPUS ». No figure is given for the coaxial or optical inputs, the six filters are counted and not named, and no NOS mode is mentioned.

facts.chip: « 2x AKM AK4493SEQ » in the specification list and « Pair of AKM AK4493S DACs » in the bullet list above it - two forms of one part on one page, both quoted, neither picked. USB receiver « Xmos XU316 ».

device_settings.why: « Digital Filters：6 Preset Filters » - a count and no names. Its sibling the H7 says exactly the same thing, and the EC Zero AKM's manual DOES name six AKM filters, so the list exists somewhere in this maker's documentation and not on this page.

_la_source_est_une_annonce_ou_un_manuel_: Shanling's product pages are image-only, so every figure comes from the maker's own announcement at /article/NNNNNN or from its manual PDF, both on en.shanling.com. No number was read off an image, and nothing is sourced to store.shanling.com. See the brand file.
_ni_DoP_ni_natif_ne_sont_dits_pour_ce_mo: DoP appears on no Shanling page or manual, and « native » only in the UA dongle manuals and in EM5. Neither is stated for this model.
_le_fabricant_separe_lENTREE_de_la_CARTE: « USB Input Hi-Res Support：32 bit / 768 kHz， DSD 512 » then « MicroSD Hi-Res Support：32 bit / 384 kHz， DSD 256 ». Two labelled ceilings, one for what arrives at the socket and one for what is read off the card, and they differ by a factor of two in both PCM and DSD. This is the distinction every portable player in this catalogue makes ambiguous and that iBasso could not even be asked about - stated here, by the maker, in two consecutive lines. `pcm_max_hz` and inputs.usb take the INPUT figure, 768 kHz, and the card's 384 is recorded nowhere because the catalogue has no field for what a device plays from its own storage. The best per-role split on any portable device in the base.
